title: Lord, I Have Made Thy Word My Choice
description: Lord, I Have Made Thy Word My Choice in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 119, part 8, headed “The word of God is the saint's portion; or, The excellency and variety of scripture”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, I have made thy word my choice, My last-ing her-i-tage; There shall my no-blest powers re-joice, My war-mest thoughts en-gage.

lines: Lord, I have made thy word my choice,
There shall my noblest powers rejoice,
I'll read the histories of thy love,
And keep thy laws in sight,
While thro' the promises I rove,
'Tis a broad land of wealth unknown
Seeds of immortal bliss are sown,
The best relief that mourners have,
Our fairest hope beyond the grave,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
